findings.evidence: Six sentinel readings in a channel whose value is 120.4 +/- 0.06 everywhere else and in all 17 other files: 999.9 at samples 113, 274, 569 and 0.0 at samples 184, 442, 578. These are out-of-range placeholders written into the record, not measurements.

After discarding the six sentinels above, tag_40's robust sigma in this file is 0.059 against 0.0148 pooled across the other files - a 4x spread increase with the median unchanged at 120.40. Block scatter climbs from 1x pooled in samples 0-100 to 3-7x for the rest of the file. tag_40 has no coupled partner in any file and nothing else in unit_14 moves, so this is the channel getting noisier, not the reference moving. Reported separately from the sentinels because the inflation survives their removal.

Eight readings are negative - -3671.8, -3646.3, -3626.1, -3675.2, -3650.7, -3678.7, -3628.4, -3622.4 at samples 76, 106, 213, 265, 551, 597, 652, 678 - while the channel's normal range is +3581..+3741. Each magnitude sits squarely inside the normal band, so the sign is wrong as written rather than the value. The surrounding samples and tag_07's partner tag_15 are undisturbed.

Median unchanged (41.00 in this file vs 41.11 pooled; block medians stay within 39.3-43.3, under 4 sd) but robust sigma is 3.36 against 0.553 pooled - a 6.1x inflation, with the changepoint at sample ~88 (block scatter 0.92, 1.17x pooled for samples 0-110, then 3.5-9.3x for the rest). tag_05 has no coupled partner in any of the 18 files and no other column in unit_14 moves, so nothing in the process is driving it. This is the class of fault that leaves the mean intact and only shows up in table B.
